import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 40

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture40

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α] (G : SimpleGraph α)

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 40](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a nontrivial connected graph `G` the size `f(G)` of a largest induced forest
satisfies `f(G) ≥ ceil((p(G) + b(G) + 1)/2)` where `p(G)` is the path cover
number and `b(G)` is the largest induced bipartite subgraph size.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture40 (h_conn : G.Connected) (h_nontrivial : 1 < Fintype.card α) :
    ⌈(((pathCoverNumber G : ℝ) + b G + 1) / 2)⌉ ≤  G.largestInducedForestSize := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture40

sources_consulted: E. DeLaViña, Graffiti.pc: A Variant of Graffiti, §2.2, p. 4: https://www.uhd.edu/documents/academics/sciences/grafvariant.pdf

could_not_verify: WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture40.conjecture40: I could not obtain Conjecture 40 itself, including its remarks and status. The cited http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/ timed out; the author's current cms.uhd.edu address redirects to an unavailable HTTPS endpoint. Internet Archive metadata identifies a 2024-05-12 snapshot, but the snapshot could not be retrieved. The accessible author paper confirms the path-cover definition, not this particular inequality, its exact hypotheses, or its present research status.
review.notes: No substantiated mathematical defect found, but source verification is incomplete. DeLaViña's paper defines the path covering number as the minimum number of vertex-disjoint paths covering the vertices, matching IsPathCover. Lean checks in /workspace/review/boundary.lean establish existence of path covers, positivity on nonempty graphs, boundedness of the forest/bipartite size sets, the invariant values on zero, one, and two vertices, and equivalence of the ceiling inequality to p + b + 1 ≤ 2*f. The explicit cardinality hypothesis follows from Nontrivial. K₂ satisfies the hypotheses and inequality; the failing zero- and one-vertex cases are excluded. An independent C++ enumeration found no failures among all 27,475 connected labelled graphs on two through six vertices. These checks do not certify agreement with the inaccessible WOWII entry or its current status.
